The covariation generator has no panel_conditions field to read. A sample series is detected from the observation text — three or more numbers in one sweep — and two series pair when they are the same length. Length is not comparability, which is why 37% of sampled covariation propositions set quantities of different kinds against each other.

4The two-step items

Every item is exactly two steps: two observations the graph already links, asked so neither answers alone. Chains are these items joined end to end, in section 5 — never one long trace.

complementary — 6 items
bioactive_ma_com_o11_o12_n18
step 1 · SEM
Many spread, dendritic platelets on 316L SS and PPAmF; fewer on BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF; a few round, unspread platelets on BVLD/NO-PPAmF
step 2 · BIO:platelet_count
Adhered platelets ~32, 41, 15.5, 11 and 5 (x1e2 cell/mm2) on 316L SS, PPAmF, BVLD-PPAmF, NO-PPAmF, BVLD/NO-PPAmF
the question, as the solver sees itWhat does each of these two measurements establish on its own about PRP/value, and what does putting them together add that neither gives alone?
generator complementarydepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength associative
key — the combining proposition
Together, the SEM morphology and the BIO platelet counts show that BVLD/NO-PPAmF has both the fewest adhered platelets (~5x1e2 cells/mm2, lowest of the five surfaces) and a morphology dominated by a few round, unspread platelets, in contrast to 316L SS and PPAmF (32 and 41x1e2 cells/mm2, many spread dendritic platelets) and to BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF alone (15.5 and 11x1e2 cells/mm2, fewer spread platelets but still present). Combining the two measurements shows a reduced platelet number (BIO) co-occurring with reduced platelet spreading/activation shape (SEM) specifically on BVLD/NO-PPAmF -- a joint reduction in adhesion and activation that neither the count alone (which says nothing about the shape/activation state of the platelets present) nor the SEM images alone (which give no quantitative count) can show.
limits
  • No statistics or error bars are reported alongside either measurement, so the apparent stepwise ordering across the five surfaces is descriptive, not tested
  • SEM morphology is reported qualitatively per surface (many/fewer/a few) and is not tied numerically to the counted platelet densities from the same fields, so the correspondence between 'few round platelets' and '5x1e2 cells/mm2' is descriptive, not a measured relationship
  • The pair says nothing about the underlying surface-chemistry or biochemical mechanism producing the suppression -- only that count and morphology move together across surfaces

bioactive_ma_com_o15_o16
step 1 · PHOTO:macro
Photographs: 316L SS and PPAmF tubes are filled by dark thrombus; BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF partly open; BVLD/NO-PPAmF lumen and foil nearly clean
step 2 · SEM
SEM: dense fibrin network with trapped cells on 316L SS and PPAmF; platelets with little fibrin on BVLD-PPAmF; fibrin strands on NO-PPAmF; almost bare BVLD/NO-PPAmF
the question, as the solver sees itWhat does each of these two measurements establish on its own about PRF/service_capability, and what does putting them together add that neither gives alone?
generator complementarydepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength descriptive
key — the combining proposition
Together, the macro photos (Observation A) and SEM (Observation B) show that gross-scale lumen patency corresponds to microscale absence of thrombogenic deposits: on 316L SS and PPAmF the lumen is filled with dark thrombus (photo) built from a dense fibrin network trapping cells (SEM); on BVLD/NO-PPAmF the lumen and foil are nearly clean (photo) and the surface is almost bare of fibrin or platelets (SEM). The pairing also distinguishes the two single-agent surfaces, which look similarly 'partly open' at macro scale but differ in microscale deposit character: BVLD-PPAmF carries platelets with little fibrin, while NO-PPAmF carries fibrin strands -- a distinction photos alone cannot make and SEM alone (without the photo's patency context) cannot connect to overall lumen openness.
limits
  • Both observations are qualitative image descriptions (extent/coverage by eye, deposit type by micrograph), not the paper's quantitative outcome measures (occlusion percentage, thrombus mass, flow retained), so this pair does not by itself establish those numeric levels
  • The images do not indicate sample size, replicate consistency, or statistical comparison across surfaces
  • Photos and SEM are taken from the same explanted segments, so they are not independent replications of the patency finding, only two scales of the same specimens
  • Neither observation establishes duration-dependence or whether the deposit pattern would change with longer shunt exposure
not identifiableWhether the near-complete cleanliness of BVLD/NO-PPAmF arises from an additive combination of the two single-agent mechanisms (platelet suppression from BVLD-PPAmF plus fibrin-strand suppression from NO-PPAmF) or from a distinct synergistic mechanism cannot be separated from these two image-based observations alone

bioactive_ma_com_o16_o17
step 1 · SEM
SEM: dense fibrin network with trapped cells on 316L SS and PPAmF; platelets with little fibrin on BVLD-PPAmF; fibrin strands on NO-PPAmF; almost bare BVLD/NO-PPAmF
step 2 · BIO:ex_vivo_shunt
Occlusion ~58, 63, 10, 7.5 and 3% (316L SS, PPAmF, BVLD-PPAmF, NO-PPAmF, BVLD/NO-PPAmF)
the question, as the solver sees itWhat does each of these two measurements establish on its own about PRF/service_capability, and what does putting them together add that neither gives alone?
generator complementarydepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength associative
key — the combining proposition
Read together across the same five surfaces, SEM morphology and ex vivo shunt occlusion percentage track each other: surfaces showing dense fibrin networks with trapped cells (316L SS, PPAmF) correspond to high occlusion (~58% and ~63%), while surfaces showing platelets with little fibrin, fibrin strands, or an almost bare surface (BVLD-PPAmF, NO-PPAmF, BVLD/NO-PPAmF) correspond to progressively lower occlusion (~10%, ~7.5%, ~3%). This lets the qualitative SEM images be interpreted as the structural counterpart of the quantitative occlusion outcome for each surface, something neither the images nor the occlusion numbers alone would tie together.
limits
  • SEM gives only a qualitative, single-time-point description of deposition (no fibrin/platelet coverage percentage), so the match to occlusion % is a pattern-level correspondence, not a measured quantitative relationship
  • Only five surfaces are compared, too few points to establish a dose-response or statistical relationship -- just a consistent ordering across the set
  • The pairing is descriptive/associative: it shows structure and occlusion outcome co-vary across surfaces, not that the fibrin/platelet deposition causally produces the occlusion level
  • BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF show different SEM morphologies (platelets with little fibrin vs. fibrin strands) yet similar occlusion (~10% vs ~7.5%), so the structure-function correspondence is not precise enough to attribute occlusion reduction to a specific surface feature
not identifiableWhether the BVLD (antithrombin) component or the NO-release component of the coating is more responsible for lowering occlusion -- BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF produce different SEM morphologies but similar occlusion (~10% vs ~7.5%), so the pair cannot separate each mechanism's individual contribution to the combined BVLD/NO-PPAmF result (~3%)

claims n20

bioactive_ma_com_o1_o2
step 1 · FTIR:GATR
PPAm IR bands assigned: N-H stretch 3350/3210, C-H stretch, -N=C=O/-C=N 2245/2180, -C=O/C=N 1645, C-N 1230 cm-1
step 2 · SIMS:ToF
Positive ToF-SIMS spectrum shows labelled N-containing ions CH4N (m/z 30), C3H9N (m/z 59) and C4H10N (m/z 72) among CxHy ions
the question, as the solver sees itWhat does each of these two measurements establish on its own about STR/chemistry/bonding, and what does putting them together add that neither gives alone?
generator complementarydepth 2lane otherdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength descriptive
key — the combining proposition
FTIR (GATR) assigns specific vibrational bands to bond types present in the PPAm film -- N-H (3350/3210 cm-1), aliphatic C-H, -N=C=O/-C=N (2245/2180 cm-1), C=O/C=N (1645 cm-1), C-N (1230 cm-1) -- while ToF-SIMS independently detects N-containing fragment ions (CH4N m/z 30, C3H9N m/z 59, C4H10N m/z 72) among the CxHy ion set at the surface. Put together, the two techniques give converging, independent confirmation that nitrogen is retained as part of the film's molecular structure and is detectable both as vibrational bonding signatures and as surface mass fragments -- a stronger basis for asserting N retention than either technique alone, since FTIR could in principle reflect subsurface/bulk species and SIMS fragment masses alone do not confirm a bonding assignment.
limits
  • ToF-SIMS fragment formulas (CH4N, C3H9N, C4H10N) are mass-only identifications and cannot by themselves specify which functional group (amine N-H vs nitrile/isocyanate vs C=O/C=N) the nitrogen belongs to, so they cannot confirm the specific bond assignments FTIR makes
  • the FTIR bands attributed to plasma-fragmentation products (-N=C=O/-C=N at 2245/2180 cm-1, C=O/C=N at 1645 cm-1) have no corresponding fragment explicitly identified in the cited SIMS ion list, so the pairing does not show that SIMS detects those specific new groups
  • neither observation gives a quantity (amount or rate) of any group, so the combination cannot establish how much N-H versus nitrile/isocyanate/C=O is present, only that N-containing species are present in both measurement modalities
  • GATR-FTIR and ToF-SIMS probe different depths/mechanisms (vibrational absorption vs surface fragment ejection), so agreement on 'N is present' does not establish the two techniques are sampling the identical molecular species
not identifiablewhether the SIMS N-containing fragments (CH4N, C3H9N, C4H10N) arise from the retained allylamine N-H/amine groups or from the newly formed nitrile/isocyanate/C=O groups produced by plasma fragmentation -- the given data cannot separate these two possible sources of the surface nitrogen signal

statementverdictevidence quoted
propositionholdsObservation A: 'PPAm IR bands assigned: N-H stretch 3350/3210, C-H stretch, -N=C=O/-C=N 2245/2180, -C=O/C=N 1645, C-N 1230 cm-1' and Observation B: 'Positive ToF-SIMS spectrum shows labelled N-containing ions CH4N (m/z 30), C3H9N (m/z 59) and C4H10N (m/z 72) among CxHy ions' -- together these are two independent, technique-distinct detections of nitrogen in the film (bond-vibration evidence vs. mass-fragment evidence), which is a reasonable basis for the stated 'converging, independent confirmation' claim; no quantity or direction is asserted beyond what the two observations support.
limit[0]holdsObservation B only reports elemental/mass formulas (CH4N, C3H9N, C4H10N) with no bonding or functional-group information, consistent with the claim that mass-only IDs cannot specify which functional group (amine vs nitrile/isocyanate vs C=O/C=N) the N belongs to.
limit[1]overreachesObservation A: '-N=C=O/-C=N 2245/2180, -C=O/C=N 1645' with no mention of plasma or fragmentation processes; Observation B lists only CH4N, C3H9N, C4H10N with no corresponding entry for these bands. The core claim (no matching SIMS fragment for these two FTIR band sets) is supported, but labeling them 'plasma-fragmentation products' attributes a formation mechanism not stated in either observation.
limit[2]holdsNeither Observation A (band positions/assignments only) nor Observation B (ion formulas and m/z values only) reports a concentration, intensity, or rate for any group, so the claim that the combination cannot establish relative amounts of N-H vs nitrile/isocyanate vs C=O is accurate.
limit[3]holdsObservation A is labelled 'FTIR:GATR' (an attenuated-total-reflectance vibrational absorption technique) and Observation B is labelled 'SIMS:ToF' (a surface secondary-ion mass spectrometry technique ejecting fragments); these are inherently different physical mechanisms/sampling depths, so agreement that 'N is present' in both does not by itself establish they sampled the same molecular species.

quantity kind: same_kind FTIR (GATR) vibrational band assignments to bond types (N-H 3350/3210, -N=C=O/-C=N 2245/2180, C=O/C=N 1645, C-N 1230 cm-1) (qualitative bond/functional-group identification via vibrational absorption spectroscopy) against ToF-SIMS positive-ion fragment identities (CH4N m/z 30, C3H9N m/z 59, C4H10N m/z 72) among CxHy ions (qualitative atomic-composition/mass identification via surface fragment ejection, with no bond-type specificity)

bioactive_ma_com_o5_o7
step 1 · FTIR:GATR
BVLD-PPAmF spectrum carries a labelled -COOH stretch (~3400 cm-1) and -C=O band (~1660 cm-1) over the PPAmF spectrum
step 2 · QCM:dissipation
QCM-D: BVLD mass rises after BVLD injection to ~0.78 ug/cm2 and settles near 0.71 after PBS rinse; 0.74 +/- 0.05 ug/cm2 annotated
the question, as the solver sees itWhat does each of these two measurements establish on its own about STR/chemistry/composition, and what does putting them together add that neither gives alone?
generator complementarydepth 2lane otherdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength associative
key — the combining proposition
Together, the FTIR chemical signature (-COOH ~3400 cm-1, -C=O ~1660 cm-1 on BVLD-PPAmF vs PPAmF) and the QCM-D areal mass trace (rise to ~0.78 ug/cm2 after BVLD injection, settling to ~0.71 after PBS rinse, 0.74 +/- 0.05 ug/cm2 annotated) support that BVLD is chemically immobilised on the coating surface and remains at ~0.74 ug/cm2 after PBS rinsing.
limits
  • FTIR alone gives no quantity and no information about whether the material survives rinsing
  • QCM-D alone quantifies retained areal mass but cannot confirm the retained mass is chemically BVLD rather than nonspecific adsorbate, buffer residue, or hydration/dissipation-associated mass
  • the pair does not establish the immobilisation mechanism (covalent bonding vs physical adsorption/entrapment)
  • QCM-D mass may include hydrated/coupled water rather than pure dry BVLD mass, a different quantity kind than the FTIR chemical-identity signal
not identifiablewhether BVLD is covalently bonded versus physically adsorbed/entrapped on the surface cannot be separated from FTIR (shows functional groups, not bond type) and QCM-D (shows retained mass, not why it is retained)

step 1 · UVVIS:chromogenic_assay
Thrombin specific activity ~0.65e-3 abs/ng/cm2 on BVLD-PPAmF and BVLD/NO-PPAmF vs ~1.3e-3 on 316L SS, PPAmF and NO-PPAmF (***)
step 2 · SEM
Many spread, dendritic platelets on 316L SS and PPAmF; fewer on BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF; a few round, unspread platelets on BVLD/NO-PPAmF
the question, as the solver sees itDoes the upstream evidence account for the downstream observation about PRP/value / PRP/value? Say what the combination supports and what it leaves open.
generator spine_edgedepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength associative
key — the combining proposition
Together, the thrombin-activity assay and the SEM morphology survey support that BVLD-bearing coatings (BVLD-PPAmF and BVLD/NO-PPAmF) both retain reduced thrombin specific activity (~0.65e-3 abs/ng/cm2, versus ~1.3e-3 on 316L SS, PPAmF, NO-PPAmF) and show reduced platelet spreading/activation on SEM (fewer, less dendritic platelets on BVLD-PPAmF; a few round, unspread platelets on BVLD/NO-PPAmF), consistent with retained anti-thrombin bioactivity accompanying suppressed platelet activation on BVLD-grafted surfaces.
limits
  • NO-PPAmF alone shows thrombin specific activity at the high, unaltered level (~1.3e-3, grouped with 316L SS and PPAmF) yet SEM still shows fewer spread platelets than on 316L SS/PPAmF, so the pairing does not show that thrombin-activity change tracks platelet suppression consistently across all four surfaces
  • the chromogenic assay is a single normalized enzymatic readout (activity per ng protein per cm2) while the SEM evidence is a qualitative/categorical description of platelet number and morphology, not a matched quantitative platelet count or activation score, so no dose-response or magnitude correlation between the two can be established
  • the greatest platelet suppression (round, unspread platelets) occurs on BVLD/NO-PPAmF, which has the same thrombin specific activity as BVLD-PPAmF alone, so the extra suppression seen with NO added cannot be attributed to a further change in thrombin activity from this pairing
not identifiablewhether platelet-adhesion/activation suppression is driven by BVLD's anti-thrombin bioactivity, by an NO-mediated pathway acting independently of thrombin activity, or by both together -- the NO-PPAmF surface shows unchanged thrombin activity but altered platelet morphology, so the two candidate mechanisms cannot be separated from this pairing

step 1 · UVVIS:chromogenic_assay
Thrombin specific activity ~0.65e-3 abs/ng/cm2 on BVLD-PPAmF and BVLD/NO-PPAmF vs ~1.3e-3 on 316L SS, PPAmF and NO-PPAmF (***)
step 2 · BIO:ELISA
Total fibrinogen (~0.10 -> ~0.053-0.06) and gamma-chain (~0.13-0.15 -> ~0.054-0.065) halve on all three functionalised coatings; BVLD/NO is not the lowest
the question, as the solver sees itDoes the upstream evidence account for the downstream observation about PRP/value / PRP/value? Say what the combination supports and what it leaves open.
generator spine_edgedepth 2lane otherdependency realinference does not followcausal strength discriminating
key — the combining proposition
Read together, the two panels show that BVLD's anti-thrombin bioactivity and the drop in fibrinogen/gamma-chain adsorption are dissociated, not co-occurring effects of a single mechanism. Thrombin specific activity falls only on the BVLD-bearing coatings (~0.65e-3 abs/ng/cm2 on BVLD-PPAmF and BVLD/NO-PPAmF vs ~1.3e-3 on 316L SS, PPAmF and NO-PPAmF), whereas total fibrinogen (~0.10 to ~0.053-0.06) and gamma-chain exposure (~0.13-0.15 to ~0.054-0.065) drop on all three functionalised coatings, including NO-PPAmF, which shows no reduction in thrombin activity, and BVLD/NO is not even the lowest for fibrinogen despite carrying the BVLD anti-thrombin effect.
limits
  • NO-PPAmF halves fibrinogen/gamma-chain exposure without any matching fall in thrombin specific activity, so retained anti-thrombin bioactivity is not necessary for the fibrinogen effect
  • BVLD/NO-PPAmF carries the BVLD anti-thrombin effect but is not the lowest for fibrinogen, so more thrombin inhibition does not track with less fibrinogen adsorption
  • the two assays measure different quantity kinds (a normalized enzymatic activity per area vs. an ELISA signal for adsorbed protein amount), so they are not on a common scale for inferring one drives the other
  • the coating groupings differ across the two observations (BVLD-bearing vs non-BVLD-bearing in A; all three functionalised coatings vs baseline in B), so a matched, like-for-like causal comparison is not set up

bioactive_ma_spi_o11_o15
step 1 · SEM
Many spread, dendritic platelets on 316L SS and PPAmF; fewer on BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF; a few round, unspread platelets on BVLD/NO-PPAmF
step 2 · PHOTO:macro
Photographs: 316L SS and PPAmF tubes are filled by dark thrombus; BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF partly open; BVLD/NO-PPAmF lumen and foil nearly clean
the question, as the solver sees itDoes the upstream evidence account for the downstream observation about PRP/value / PRF/service_capability? Say what the combination supports and what it leaves open.
generator spine_edgedepth 2lane FMdependency realinference follows, weaklycausal strength conditional mechanism
key — the combining proposition
Across the same set of surfaces, the SEM platelet pattern (many spread, dendritic platelets on 316L SS and PPAmF; fewer on BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF; only a few round, unspread platelets on BVLD/NO-PPAmF) tracks the same ranking seen in the tube photographs (dark thrombus filling 316L SS and PPAmF tubes; BVLD-PPAmF and NO-PPAmF tubes only partly open; BVLD/NO-PPAmF lumen and foil nearly clean). Put together, the two panels support that the surface ordering for platelet adhesion/activation matches the surface ordering for macroscopic thrombus occlusion, consistent with platelet spreading/activation being the mechanism behind the visible difference in thrombus formation, with the combination BVLD/NO-PPAmF showing the least of both.
limits
  • Both readouts are qualitative/visual categories (spread-dendritic vs few-round-unspread on SEM; filled vs partly-open vs nearly-clean on photos), not counted or quantified, so only an ordering across this small set of surfaces is supported, not a dose-response or magnitude relationship.
